title: Principal Fitting ideal gives generators after removing its torsion
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative local ring, let $M$ be a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and let $k\geq0$. Use the presentation-independent Fitting ideal $\operatorname{Fit}_k(M)$ of [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change]. If $\operatorname{Fit}_k(M)=(f)$ for $f\in A$, then $M/\{x\in M\mid fx=0\}$ can be generated by $k$ elements.

proof.text: Put $T=\{x\in M\mid fx=0\}$; this is a submodule since multiplication by $f$ is $A$-linear. If $f=0$, then $T=M$ and $M/T=0$ is generated by the empty family. Hence assume $f\ne0$. Choose a generating family $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ of $M$ using [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], with associated surjection $\pi:A^{\oplus n}\twoheadrightarrow M$. If $n\le k$, their images already generate $M/T$ with at most $k$ elements. Henceforth $r=n-k>0$.

source.place: Tag 080Z, lemma-principal-fitting-ideal: generating family and boundary cases

proof.text: By [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change], $(f)=\operatorname{Fit}_k(M)$ is generated by the $r$-minors of $r\times n$ matrices with rows in $\ker\pi$. Membership of $f$ in this generated ideal gives a finite expression $f=\sum_{\ell=1}^t a_\ell\delta_\ell$ with each $\delta_\ell$ such a minor. Write $\delta_\ell=b_\ell f$, since it lies in $(f)$. Some $b_\ell$ is a unit: otherwise all $b_\ell$ lie in the unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, so $s=\sum_\ell a_\ell b_\ell\in\mathfrak m$. But $(1-s)f=0$ and $1-s$ is a unit (it is outside $\mathfrak m$), contradicting $f\ne0$. Select such a minor $\delta=uf$, with $u$ a unit. This is the elementary local-ring argument underlying the Nakayama invocation in the source.

source.place: Tag 080Z, lemma-principal-fitting-ideal: selection of one generating minor; elementary coefficient proof of the local Nakayama consequence

proof.text: Choose its $r$ relation rows and order the generator coordinates so that their matrix is $Z=(D\ E)$, with $D$ square of size $r$, $E$ of size $r\times k$, and $\det D=uf$ (absorbing a permutation sign into the unit $u$ if necessary). Thus each row says $\sum_{j=1}^rD_{ij}x_j+\sum_{l=1}^kE_{il}x_{r+l}=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-matrix-adjugate-identity], multiplying these relations by $H=\operatorname{adj}(D)$ gives the relation matrix $HZ=(uf I_r\ HE)$. Its entry $(i,l)$ in the last block is $\sum_{j=1}^r(-1)^{i+j}\det(D^{(j,i)})E_{jl}$.

source.place: Tag 080Z, lemma-principal-fitting-ideal: adjugate calculation; transposed form of Algebra Tag 080R, lemma-matrix-right-inverse

proof.text: Let $D_i(E_l)$ denote $D$ with its $i$th column replaced by the $l$th column of $E$. In the Leibniz formula of [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant], group the permutations by the row $j$ used in column $i$. The terms for fixed $j$ have the common factor $E_{jl}$; deleting that row and column leaves precisely the determinant of $D^{(j,i)}$, with sign $(-1)^{i+j}$. Therefore $\det D_i(E_l)=\sum_j(-1)^{i+j}\det(D^{(j,i)})E_{jl}=(HE)_{il}$. The selected columns are $r$ distinct columns of $Z$, so this determinant is, up to column-order sign, an $r$-minor from the original presentation. By [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change], it belongs to $(f)$. Choose $c_{il}\in A$ with $(HE)_{il}=fc_{il}$ for each of the finitely many entries. Thus $HZ=f(u I_r\ C)$, where $C=(c_{il})$.

source.place: Tag 080Z, lemma-principal-fitting-ideal: all other minors are multiples of f; Algebra Tag 080R, displayed cofactor computation, transposed

proof.text: The rows of $HZ$ are linear combinations of relation rows, hence for every $1\le i\le r$ one has $f(ux_i+\sum_{l=1}^k c_{il}x_{r+l})=0$. Thus $y_i=ux_i+\sum_l c_{il}x_{r+l}$ belongs to $T$. In $M/T$, multiplication by $u^{-1}$ gives $\bar x_i=-\sum_l u^{-1}c_{il}\bar x_{r+l}$. Since all $\bar x_j$ generate $M/T$, the last $k$ of them generate it. This also treats $k=0$: then every $\bar x_i=0$ and the quotient is zero.
